extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies and NEPA practitioners (agency NEPA staff, counsel, environmental consultants, and public engagement officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for Federal agencies to prepare and process NEPA environmental reviews (EAs/EISs), including documentation, timing, modeling, public engagement, emergency procedures, and agency procedures. Covers obligations under CEQ regulations to ensure professional integrity, data reliability, and public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of assumptions and limitations of models and methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall explain relevant assumptions or limitations of any models or methodologies on which they rely for their analyses; CEQ includes the sentence at the end of §1506.6(b) changing 'should' to 'shall'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement supports integrity of discussions and analyses in environmental documents so decision makers and the public can assess reliability. It applies to mathematical or other models that project possible future outcomes and agencies must disclose underlying relevant assumptions or limitations of those models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may undertake new research when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule strikes the 2020 sentence stating agencies are not required to undertake new research; CEQ explains agencies sometimes will need to undertake research to meet statutory NEPA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ disagrees that deletion implies agencies must always do new research; rather agencies retain judgment to determine when new research is necessary or appropriate. Agencies should continue to rely on existing information when able, but may develop new data specific to an action's circumstances (e.g., affected environment) when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability of data and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Any data or resources an agency relies upon, whether existing or new, must be reliable (consistent with section 102(2)(E) of NEPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ states section 102(2)(E) does not limit to only existing data; agencies must ensure reliability of any information used in analyses. CEQ also adds a regulatory requirement that agencies 'make use of reliable data and resources' in §1507.2(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify methodologies and cite sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to identify any methodologies used and make explicit reference to the scientific and other sources relied upon for conclusions in the environmental document, which agencies may place in an appendix (moved to §1506.6(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This improves organizational clarity and codifies typical agency practice; citations and methodological descriptions may be included in appendices to the environmental document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use projections where appropriate for reasonably foreseeable effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to use projections when evaluating reasonably foreseeable effects, including climate change-related effects, where appropriate (proposed §1502.23(c) included in final rule at §1506.6(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projections may employ models that project a range of possible future outcomes; inclusion of climate-change related effects is an example, not an elevation over other effects. Projections are required only where an agency considers them appropriate; agencies should explain basis and assumptions for relying on projections and may scale projections to localized geographic scope when available and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of assumptions and limitations for projections and models
rubrics_metrics.description: When agencies use projections or models to analyze reasonably foreseeable effects, they must disclose the assumptions and limitations underlying any projection or model upon which the agency relies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Climate projections can vary by geography, location, and future GHG emissions assumptions; agencies should disclose these factors. Models analyzing ranges of outcomes are acceptable provided assumptions/limitations are disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use high-quality information as modeling improves
rubrics_metrics.description: As modeling techniques advance, agencies should continue to rely on high-quality information when evaluating reasonably foreseeable effects (consistent with §1506.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ expects modeling techniques to improve and anticipates agencies will use improved, high-quality information in future analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEQ guidance must be consistent with NEPA and the regulations; rule prevails over guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ will provide additional guidance as needed concerning NEPA implementation; any such guidance will be consistent with NEPA, the CEQ regulations, and other applicable requirements. If there is a conflict between existing guidance and an issued final rule, the final rule will prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Future guidance might update existing CEQ guidance or add new material, but cannot override the final rule. CEQ considered but declined to codify detailed modeling quality or transparency standards in the regulations, reserving such issues for potential guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not substitute separate regulatory rulemaking processes for NEPA
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ removes 'Proposals for regulations' (§1506.9 (2020)) to avoid confusion that processes of a separate rulemaking could substitute for NEPA; courts have questioned whether separate regulatory processes can substitute for NEPA in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should integrate NEPA into their processes and may combine documents or procedural steps where appropriate, but must not treat another agency's permit or rulemaking process as a substitute for a proper NEPA analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: File adoptions of EISs with EPA (notification requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must notify EPA when they adopt an EIS consistent with §1506.3(b); CEQ adds paragraph (c) in the final rule to require agencies to file an adoption of an EIS with EPA consistent with current practice and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must occur at the same time as adoption (CEQ declines to add a separate 'timely' window). Filing adoption with EPA ensures appropriate comment/review periods and transparency about EIS status across the Federal Government. Only adoptions under §1506.3(b)(1) require filing with EPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory minimum timing periods between draft EIS/final EIS and ROD
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ changed 'may not' to 'shall not' to make clear that the minimum periods between a draft EIS and ROD (paragraph (b)(1)) and between a final EIS and ROD (paragraph (b)(2)) are mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retains the longstanding minimum timeframes (including the minimum 45-day public comment period for draft EISs) to ensure transparent opportunities for public input. CEQ declines requests to shorten these timeframes but encourages agencies to improve notification practices (e.g., distribution lists) rather than extend comment periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must notify the public of opportunities for public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must notify the public of opportunities for public comment and are encouraged to consider effective and efficient notification methods to ensure interested parties receive timely notice (see §1501.9 and §1503.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ intends revisions to §1501.9 regarding public engagement to facilitate notification. Agencies have discretion to consider special or unique circumstances for accepting comments outside the public comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review processes may run concurrently with ROD wait period
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ updated references to 'administrative review processes' (e.g., appeals, objections, protests) and clarified such a process may be initiated before or after filing and publication of a final EIS with EPA; the administrative review period and the 30-day period for when a ROD can be issued may run concurrently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change reflects existing agency practices (e.g., Forest Service objections process) and provides flexibility so agencies can avoid inefficiency by filing EISs and concluding administrative processes without unnecessary sequential waits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to accommodate agency-specific administrative review procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies with administrative review procedures (e.g., objections, protests) may file final EISs with EPA and issue a ROD at times that align with those procedures to avoid inefficiency and accommodate agency authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Forest Service objections (36 CFR part 218) and BLM protest procedures; CEQ revised text to better accommodate such existing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult CEQ on alternative arrangements for emergencies (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: For actions with significant effects, agencies shall consult with CEQ on alternative arrangements for emergencies (CEQ changed 'should' to 'shall').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation ensures alternative arrangements are limited to necessary emergency actions, that the public is appropriately notified and involved, and that arrangements are not used to circumvent NEPA. CEQ also revised 'will' to 'shall' to clarify regulatory requirement language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative arrangements are not waivers of NEPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative arrangements during emergencies establish an alternative means for NEPA compliance and are not a waiver; other actions remain subject to NEPA review 'consistent with this subchapter'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ does not have authority to exempt agency actions from NEPA; alternative arrangements allow agencies to act swiftly while meeting statutory obligations. Agencies may consult CEQ where unsure whether alternative arrangements or an EA are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies retain discretion for emergency actions without significant environmental effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with longstanding practice, agencies have discretion to determine how to proceed with emergency actions that do not have significant environmental effects (which would ordinarily be analyzed through an EA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may continue to consult CEQ in uncertain cases; some agencies include emergency procedures in their NEPA procedures and CEQ encourages doing so where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative approaches provision not adopted; existing mechanisms provide flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ considered and proposed a new §1506.12 to allow modification requests for innovative approaches to NEPA compliance, but commenters opposed and CEQ is not including the provision in the final rule; instead the final rule relies on programmatic reviews, tailored agency procedures, and new methods for establishing/adopting CEs to provide flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ found the proposed innovation provision lacked sufficient guideposts and could cause litigation or delay; agencies should use the mechanisms provided in the final rule to innovate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and applicability to ongoing actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1506.12 requires agencies to comply with the regulations for proposed actions begun after the effective date of the final rule. Agencies may determine on a case-by-case basis whether applying provisions of the revised regulations to ongoing reviews will facilitate more effective and efficient processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency NEPA procedures remain in effect until revised under §1507.3, but should be read in concert with the final rule. CEQ notes Fiscal Responsibility Act amendments to NEPA were effective upon enactment and may apply to ongoing reviews. Agencies would not need to redo or supplement completed NEPA reviews (e.g., where CE, FONSI, or ROD issued).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must comply with CEQ regulations but may adapt procedures to other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to comply with CEQ regulations and have flexibility to adapt implementing procedures to the requirements of other applicable laws (restoring language from 1978 regulations in §1507.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restores longstanding approach allowing agencies to tailor procedures to unique missions while still complying with NEPA and CEQ regulations; agencies are encouraged to engage in early coordination to prevent delays and reconcile processes with other agencies where appropriate (§1507.3(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a systematic, interdisciplinary approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to fulfill the requirements of section 102(2)(A) of NEPA to use a systematic, interdisciplinary approach in preparing environmental documents (moved into §1507.2(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This emphasizes agencies' responsibilities to integrate multiple disciplines to inform NEPA analyses and decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate senior agency official and Chief Public Engagement Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must designate a senior agency official responsible for overall agency NEPA compliance and must identify a Chief Public Engagement Officer responsible for facilitating community engagement across the agency and, where appropriate, providing technical assistance to communities (§1507.2(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarifies the Officer's role is to facilitate community engagement in environmental reviews and does not make the Officer responsible for all agency engagement. Departments may have subunit officials or officers with oversight by a department-level official; senior agency official should be 'an official of assistant secretary rank or higher (or equivalent)'. Agencies may designate current employees to serve and CEQ may provide future guidance on role expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare environmental documents with professional integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to prepare environmental documents with professional integrity consistent with section 102(2)(D) of NEPA (new paragraph (e) in §1507.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds this to emphasize scientific and professional integrity in documentation; related requirements (e.g., disclosure of assumptions, use of reliable data) support this obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study, develop, and describe technically and economically feasible alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to study, develop, and describe technically and economically feasible alternatives, consistent with section 102(2)(F) of NEPA (new paragraph (g) in §1507.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinforces the statutory obligation to consider feasible alternatives in environmental analyses and requires agencies to document those alternatives in environmental documents.
